rv.q: Simply staged – a large, all-embracing cream leather chair, a small table with some family photographs, and a lamp – Jessica just sits and tells us her story, and her story is quite captivating! She is a middle-class, politically conservative (that is, Republican) Mormon who volunteers once a week at the local school.
Even to the end, Martin sells her role perfectly, giving Grindr Mom a sheen of warmth and intimacy that the script alone does not deserve.
For me, this was a disappointing miss which fell well short of those efforts.
Grindr Mom deserves to be far more than a casual hook-up; it’s the kind of show worth coming back to again and again.
Grindr Mom is itself a versatile comedy with much laughter and intrigue.

cn.t: Jessica Martin charms in this one-woman show about a Mormon mother navigating her gay son's world via Grindr, though critics split on whether the premise delivers enough substance beyond its initial novelty.
